Imagine you are managing the distribution of critical medical supplies across eight cities in a region. Each city has a specific supply or demand for these supplies, and your goal is to ensure that all cities receive the necessary resources while minimizing the total transportation cost. The transportation network connects these cities, and each route has a specific cost per unit of supply shipped, as well as a maximum capacity limit.

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    net_supply = d["net_supply"]
    cost = d["cost"]
    capacity = d["capacity"]

    nodes = sorted(net_supply.keys())
    arcs = list(cost.keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---- Sets ----
    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes, ordered=True)
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2, ordered=True)

    # ---- Variables ----
    # Non-negativity and capacity are enforced via bounds and an explicit
    # capacity constraint (both stated in the text).
    def _x_bounds(m, i, j):
        return (0, capacity[(i, j)])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=_x_bounds)

    # ---- Objective ----
    def _obj_expr(m):
        return sum(cost[(i, j)] * m.x[(i, j)] for (i, j) in m.A)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=_obj_expr(model), sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- Constraints ----

    # Flow balance: outflow - inflow = net_supply (surplus positive, demand negative)
    def _flow_balance_rule(m, k):
        out_sum = sum(m.x[(k, j)] for (i, j) in arcs if i == k)
        in_sum = sum(m.x[(i, k)] for (i, j) in arcs if j == k)
        return out_sum - in_sum == net_supply[k]

    model.flow_balance = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=_flow_balance_rule)

    # Capacity limit per route: x_ij <= cap_ij
    def _capacity_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[(i, j)] <= capacity[(i, j)]

    model.capacity_limit = pyo.Constraint(model.A, rule=_capacity_rule)

    return model
